results.draft_locus: Worked Example: The Launch Queue, Diagnosed ¶4
results.quote: Three product teams came to the same 2024 review asking for engineers.
results.finding: No 2024 review has been introduced: the only review mentioned so far is 'the review two quarters later', after the fix. Both readers could not tell which review is meant or whether it came before or after the fix, and the paragraph steps back in time after the results (6, 8, under 7 days). Reader 1: 'I could not tell whether this is Dario's diagnosis or a later meeting.' Name the review where Dario makes his choice (¶3) so that 'the same review' has a referent. Both readers also suggest the table before the results, which would be a change of spec order (p28/p29); the local fix does not need it.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, section 3 item 1 (a): 'No 2024 review has been mentioned... I could not tell which review, or whether this happened before or after the fix.'
results.waived_by: Author (Željko Obrenović), 2026-11-19, decision 'waive by rule' under the rule 'max two rounds per chapter': the unit was revised after round 2 to address this finding and was not re-checked by fresh readers.

results.quote: A constraint also moves without being relieved, when capacity arrives somewhere else in the flow.
results.finding: The opening says the constraint moves, but the paragraph shows queues growing at review and launch, the checking steps: if a check is already the constraint, it has not moved but got worse, and that the constraint is a check is assumed, not stated. Reader 1: 'I was unsure which move is meant' (the previous section also left Corvane's constraint at judgment). The prose should say which case is meant: where writing was the slowest step the constraint moves to the checks, where a check already was, its queue lengthens. The wording 'moves it without any relief' comes from the spec's transition, but the paragraph can be made clear without changing the order or the units.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, section 3 item 3 (a): 'The opening sentence left me unsure whether the constraint moves here or only its queue grows.'
results.waived_by: Author (Željko Obrenović), 2026-11-19, decision 'waive by rule' under the rule 'max two rounds per chapter': the unit was revised after round 2 to address this finding and was not re-checked by fresh readers.

results.draft_locus: Closing Part I: Corvane's Slowdown Without a Villain ¶1
results.quote: [[cognitive-load-and-team-boundaries]] explains why a release needed an outside check at all: teams cut by headcount, and not along the fracture planes where the domain, the rate of change or the risk differs, own parts they cannot change without touching another team's.
results.finding: Both readers went back and could not reconcile this cause of the outside check with the one given in Setting the Scene ('Corvane had no agreed test of readiness that a product team could run itself') and with 'The product teams understood their own changes, so the queue was not short of attention.' The two read as rival causes. They are compatible (entangled ownership is why a change needed a check from outside the team; the missing agreed test is why that check was done by hand at Platform), but the draft does not say so and 'at all' sharpens the conflict. Note for the author: both causes stand in the spec (p04 and p33 evidence) without a stated relation, and p33 was already changed once after round 1; one linking clause in the prose is enough, no reordering.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, section 3 item 4 (a): 'I could not reconcile the two causes.'
results.waived_by: Author (Željko Obrenović), 2026-11-19, decision 'waive by rule' under the rule 'max two rounds per chapter': the unit was revised after round 2 to address this finding and was not re-checked by fresh readers.

results.draft_locus: Where the Sources Disagree: Fix the Team or Fix the Flow ¶2
results.quote: Relieve the constraint first, in one of three ways: add people, move scope away, or limit what reaches it.
results.finding: Reader 2 (a): the preceding section offered two reliefs (people, scope), so the reader went back to look for a third; the worked example then returns to two ('A team that is falling behind needs people or less scope') and the checklist has three. Reader 1 raised a different point about the same sentence and rated it (b), so this is not corroborated. Marking limiting intake as the new, third way when it first appears would remove the doubling back.
